---
title: Component Overrides
description: Globally override how Puzzle renders links and images to integrate with routers and frameworks.
---

Puzzle components are router- and framework-independent. The `components` prop on `Theme` lets you provide the link and image implementations your application uses, and every Puzzle component that renders a link or image picks them up automatically.

## ThemeComponents

```tsx
type ThemeComponents = {
  link?: ThemeLinkComponent;
  image?: ThemeImageComponent;
};
```

## Link overrides

A link override is either a component that follows the standard `href` contract, or a configuration object for components that use a different destination prop:

```tsx
type ThemeLinkComponentConfig = {
  component: ElementType;
  /** The prop used for the destination. Defaults to "href". */
  hrefProp?: "href" | "to";
};
```

### TanStack Router

TanStack Router's `Link` uses `to` instead of `href`:

```tsx
import { Theme } from "@puzzle/theme";
import { Link } from "@tanstack/react-router";

<Theme components={{ link: { component: Link, hrefProp: "to" } }}>
  <App />
</Theme>;
```

### Next.js

Next.js `Link` already follows the `href` contract, so the component reference is enough:

```tsx
import Link from "next/link";

<Theme components={{ link: Link }}>
  <App />
</Theme>;
```

Passing `null` resets the override to the native `<a>` element.

## Image overrides

By default Puzzle renders native `<img>` elements. Override this with a framework image component, such as Next.js `Image` or a custom CDN component:

```tsx
import Image from "next/image";

<Theme components={{ image: Image }}>
  <App />
</Theme>;
```

Passing `null` resets the override to the native `<img>` element.

## Server component boundaries

When passing components through a React Server Component boundary, pass a component reference exported from a `"use client"` module rather than defining the component inline.

## Scoping

Component overrides are provided through React context by `Theme`, so they follow the component tree rather than the CSS scope. A nested `Theme` with its own `components` prop replaces the overrides for its subtree.
